response.internal_assessment: The RoboRide price drop to $0.12 per mile is the kind of news that used to make me nervous — another shift, another thing to evaluate. But I made that evaluation four ticks ago. I am car-free. The service is real, it works, and it now costs me a third less than when I started using it. What I notice, sitting with this news, is not anxiety but something quieter: a sense of confirmation. I made the right call, and I made it carefully, and the world is continuing to move in the direction I moved. The coverage expanding to residential areas matters too — that was one of the early practical concerns, whether it would actually reach my part of Millfield. It does, and it goes further now. The delivery partnership is interesting. I had not thought about using it for small purchases I would previously have driven for. That may simplify a few things. None of this requires a decision from me. I have already decided. What I am attending to now is not my own transportation situation — that is settled — but what is happening to the people around me who are still in the middle of their disruptions. Betty Kowalski is still stressed. I visited her last tick and I meant what I did. I will keep showing up. The word about Tamika Jefferson is ambiguous but she is a car salesperson in a world where car sales are collapsing — whatever change she is making, it is probably not optional. I do not know her well, but I know her. I will pay attention.
response.inbox_interpretation: The price drop to $0.12 confirms and extends the transition I have already completed — it is a personal financial benefit, not a new decision point. The 7% RoboRide usage rate is interesting context: still low, which means most people around me have not yet done what I did. Some of them are probably at tick 1 or 2 of where I was, sitting with the same fears I had. The stressed mood around Betty is consistent with what I saw in tick 7. The word-of-mouth about Tamika is incomplete — 'some kind of change' — but her profession is auto sales and the market is unmistakably contracting. She may be adapting, may be exiting, may be struggling. The word cut off before I could hear what the change was. I am going to sit with that incomplete sentence rather than fill in the blanks. The spending index at 42 and employment at 73 are macro signals, not new information. The community is in sustained stress. Nothing has resolved.

chosen_actions.description: Use my slot at the Community Center transportation session this week — the one I offered to co-facilitate last tick — to explicitly update my remarks to include the new RoboRide pricing. The price drop to $0.12 per mile and the residential coverage expansion are materially important for older adults and people on fixed incomes who were on the fence. I will not oversell the service. I will say: here is what it cost when I started, here is what it costs now, here is what that means in monthly dollars if you make four trips a week, here is the 8-minute wait time. I will still bring the printed one-page summary I wrote. I will revise the cost figures this morning before I print. I am a retired teacher. Keeping materials current is basic practice.

resources.detail: 6 hours including session preparation, revised printed materials, and facilitation at community center

chosen_actions.reasoning: I committed to this in tick 7. The price drop makes the session more timely, not less. The only change is that I need to update the cost figures on the handout before I print it. Seven percent of people using robotaxis means ninety-three percent have not yet made this transition. Some of them are in that room. Some of them have the same 2am fear I had. I can speak to that fear from direct experience, and I can now tell them the service is cheaper than it was when I made the decision. That is a useful thing to say.

chosen_actions.description: Stop by Betty's Diner again this week. I went last tick and I will go again — not to hover, not to perform concern, but because sustained presence is different from a single visit. A single visit can be curiosity. Coming back is a relationship. I will order a meal, tip well, and if Betty has bandwidth to talk I will be there for it. If she is slammed, I will eat my food and leave without demanding her attention. I will also mention, if it comes up naturally, that I have heard the RoboRide delivery partnership has started — not as a business suggestion she did not ask for, but because it might be worth knowing that robotaxis can now deliver food, which could be either competition or opportunity depending on how she wants to think about it. I will not frame it for her. I will just mention it exists.

resources.detail: Meal, coffee, generous tip at Betty's Diner on Auto Row

chosen_actions.reasoning: Betty is stressed. The inbox confirms it again this tick. I visited last tick and I intend to keep showing up. The delivery partnership is new information that might be relevant to her business situation — not advice, just information. She has been running a diner on Auto Row for years. She knows her own situation far better than I do. What I can offer is presence and a paying customer, and I can do that without making it about me.

chosen_actions.description: Send Tamika Jefferson a brief, direct note — by text, since that is how people our age communicate when we know each other professionally but not intimately. Not a long message. Something like: 'Tamika, I heard you may be working through some changes. I don't know your situation and I won't pretend to. But I've been through a transition myself this year that I didn't expect to manage as well as I did, and if you ever want to talk through anything — not about cars, just about navigating a shift — I'm around. Dorothy.' That is the whole message. I am not offering to fix her situation. I am not networking. I am acknowledging that I have heard something is changing for her and leaving the door open. She can ignore it or she can respond. Either way I will have said what I wanted to say.

resources.detail: Brief personal note by text, no money involved

chosen_actions.reasoning: The word-of-mouth was incomplete but it pointed at Tamika making some kind of change. She is a car salesperson. The auto sector in Millfield is in real pain. I do not know her situation well enough to offer anything practical, but I know what it felt like to be at the beginning of a transition I was not sure I could manage, and I know the difference between someone reaching out and no one reaching out. The message costs me nothing and may matter to her. I will send it.

chosen_actions.description: Use the RoboRide delivery partnership, newly announced, to consolidate two errands I would have made separate trips for — a pharmacy pickup and a small grocery run — into one delivery order each this week. I am testing whether the delivery function actually works in my residential area, what the interface looks like, and whether this is something I can teach other people at the community center. This is not a lifestyle change. I already use RoboRide for transport. This is an extension into a new use case, which I want to evaluate on its own terms before I recommend it to anyone. At $0.12 per mile plus whatever delivery fee applies, it is likely cheaper than a ride for a small errand. I will take notes on what works and what does not.

resources.detail: Pharmacy and grocery items received via RoboRide delivery; delivery fees estimated at $5-8 total. Net goods received, small fee paid.

chosen_actions.reasoning: The delivery partnership is new this tick. My process with RoboRide has been: learn it myself, test it, verify it works, then share what I know. I did that with the ride service over ticks 1-5. I should do the same with delivery before I say anything to others about it. The practical test also reduces a small errand burden. If it works, I have new material for the community center session. If it does not work, I know not to recommend it.

response.inner_monologue: The price dropping again should feel like a windfall but mostly it feels like confirmation — the kind you get when a decision you made carefully turns out to have been right, and the rightness is quiet rather than triumphant. I am thinking about Tamika. I do not know what she is walking into, but I know what it feels like to stand at the edge of something you have built your identity around and realize it may not hold, and I know the difference between being alone in that moment and having someone say: I see you, I don't have answers, but I'm here. That is the whole message I want to send her. I spent five ticks looking inward. I have had two ticks now of looking outward. The outward work is not finished.
